subject: Post-demo recap: GDPR intake, DPA request & SCC module clarification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsentry.io>, legal@medsentry.io
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo recap: GDPR intake, DPA request & SCC module clarification

Hi Elena / MedSentry legal team,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can keep legal + security moving: 

Summary from call:
- Product: Redwood inference runtime + Private (VPC) option looked like a good fit for your PHI-ish workloads.
- Compliance asks you raised: SOC 2 report, DPA with SCCs for EU data, and a vendor security questionnaire.
- Data-role question: you asked whether MedSentry will be controller or processor and which SCC module applies.

What we attached / are sharing now:
- MedSentry_DPA_Request_20260829.pdf (your intake form populated with the fields we discussed)
- MedSentry_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_20260829.xlsx (vendor questionnaire stub for your team to start)

Initial positions / clarifications from Redwood:
- Typical posture: Redwood generally operates as a data processor when we host customer workloads on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we can discuss controller responsibilities, but standard engagement is processor.
- SCC modules: We typically propose the EU SCCs Module 2 (processor) when we act as processor. If you require Module 1/Module 3 variants, please flag — happy to have legal weigh in.
- SOC 2: we can share our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. If you need the SOC 2 plus any additional attestation for healthcare, let us know specifics.

Proposed next steps and owners:
1) MedSentry: confirm intended data role (controller vs. processor) for the Redwood scope and confirm SCC module preference — Elena/legal target: by Tue 2026-09-01.
2) Redwood legal: Lauren to propose DPA + SCC module language and confirm if processor-only stance is acceptable; I’ll loop her in.
3) Security questionnaire: Monica will start the vendor questionnaire and return the completed sheet in 3 business days.
4) SOC 2: I will send SOC 2 access link after we complete an NDA (or share via secure link if you already have one).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call next week (I’m proposing Wed 2026-09-02 14:00 CEST / 08:00 EDT). Please confirm.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Lauren and Monica on the legal/security artifacts.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: GDPR intake, DPA request & SCC module clarification

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick responses from our side: 

- Role: We believe MedSentry will be the controller for patient data collected by our application; Redwood would be a processor for the inference calls you host. I will confirm formally with procurement/legal but plan for processor-to-controller relationship.
- SCC module: If Redwood is a processor, Module 2 sounds appropriate. We will double-check with our privacy counsel — will confirm by Tue 2026-09-01 as requested.
- SOC 2: We need a copy of your SOC 2 Type II and the dates covered. We have an NDA template we normally send; I can loop procurement if needed.
- Questionnaire: Thanks for the spreadsheet — I’ll have our security team kick it off and share any higher-priority questions.

Availability: Wed 2026-09-02 14:00 CEST works for a short call; I’ve tentatively booked the slot. Please send an invite and agenda.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of IT & Security Operations
MedSentry

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: legal@medsentry.io, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsentry.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: GDPR intake, DPA request & SCC module clarification

Elena / MedSentry legal team — looping in from Redwood legal. Thanks for the quick note and the confirmation that MedSentry expects to be controller. A few clarifications and proposed legal positions to speed review: 

1) Redwood role: our standard commercial and hosting model positions Redwood as a processor for customer data when we host inference workloads. That said, Redwood is open to contract language clarifying responsibilities (e.g., security controls, subprocessors list, deletion/return of data) — we are not seeking to be a controller for your customer data.

2) SCC modules: for processor relationships we will follow the EU SCCs Module 2 (processor) clauses. If MedSentry requires Module 1 (controller to controller) or Module 3 (controller to processor with different annexes), please confirm and provide the rationale; we can escalate to our compliance team but may need additional time.

3) DPA: I’ve attached a pointer to our DPA template here: https://redwood.example.com/dpa-template/RDW-DPA-v3.pdf — we can accept limited edits that are consistent with our security posture. I recommend a short redline rather than an entirely new draft to move faster.

4) SOC 2 access: we can share our SOC 2 report under NDA. If MedSentry wants the report plus SOC 2 bridge letters or more healthcare-specific attestations, please list those items and a target timeline.

Next steps (legal timeline):
- MedSentry confirms SCC module preference and whether any custom clauses are needed (target: 2026-09-01).
- If Module 2 is confirmed, Redwood legal will propose a DPA redline within 3 business days of receiving any redline requests.
- If MedSentry requires additional attestations, please provide the specifics and we will route to compliance for feasibility checks (timeline ~5 business days).

Happy to jump on a call Wed 2026-09-02 with both teams — I’ll be on to handle any DPA/SCC questions.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
